DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## What the author says the comparison shows

1. A two-month live trial with about 5,000 randomly allocated parcels per carrier gives a fair head-to-head.
2. ParcelLine is cheapest on the 70/30 weight mix, saving about £35,000–£76,000 a year.
3. All three carriers cleared the 95% on-time threshold.
4. ParcelLine's tracking app roughly halved "where is my order?" (WISMO) enquiries.
5. The 12-month term gives flexibility.

The trial design (claim 1) is a real strength, and the price arithmetic (claim 2) is correct. But the trial results contradict the recommendation:

- **ParcelLine failed two of the four stated requirements.** Its on-time rate and its damage rate were both below the paper's own standards.
- **ParcelLine is the most expensive option once damage and loss are counted.** The paper sets the cost of each damaged or lost parcel at £48.
- **The drop in contacts can't be credited to the app.** ParcelLine parcels also carried a new delivery text message for half the trial.

## Checks that pass

- **Weighted prices:** SwiftDrop £3.55, ParcelLine £3.48, Meridian £3.63.
- **Monthly costs:** £149,100, £146,160 and £152,460.
- **Savings:** £2,940 and £6,300 a month, which is £35,280 and £75,600 a year.
- **Contact saving:** 5 fewer contacts per 1,000 parcels × 42 (thousand parcels a month) × £3.20 = £672 a month against SwiftDrop. Against Meridian it is £538.

## ParcelLine fails the requirements

Section 2 sets the requirements as on-time delivery of at least 95% and damage below 0.5%.

| Carrier | On-time (≥ 95%) | Damage (< 0.5%) |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | 96.2% ✓ | 0.4% ✓ |
| **ParcelLine** | **93.1% ✗** | **0.9% ✗** |
| Meridian | 97.5% ✓ | 0.3% ✓ |

Section 3 says "on-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers", and the author's description repeats this. Table 1 shows otherwise. The damage requirement isn't mentioned again after Section 2.

These gaps are not trial noise. With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, ParcelLine's on-time shortfall against SwiftDrop is around 7 standard errors, and its damage gap is about 3. The differences in lost parcels, by contrast, rest on single-digit counts (roughly 1–4 lost parcels per carrier) and can't separate the carriers.

## Total cost, including damage and loss

The paper prices each damaged or lost parcel at £48 but never applies that figure. At 42,000 parcels a month:

| Carrier | Delivery cost | Damaged + lost parcels | Damage/loss cost | **Total per month** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £149,100 | 168 + 13 | £8,670 | **£157,770** |
| ParcelLine | £146,160 | 378 + 34 | £19,760 | **£165,920** |
| Meridian | £152,460 | 126 + 8 | £6,450 | **£158,910** |

ParcelLine costs about **£8,100 a month more than SwiftDrop (~£98,000 a year)** and about £7,000 a month more than Meridian. The claimed saving reverses. Adding WISMO handling costs at the trial rates changes this by only a few hundred pounds a month and leaves the order unchanged. The headline also counts nothing for one-star reviews, which the paper says damage causes most often.

## The contact reduction is confounded

Section 5 credits ParcelLine's app, then mentions that from 1 May, ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That covers half the trial, so the two effects can't be separated. The text is also being rolled out to all carriers, so any advantage it gave may disappear.

ParcelLine's lower WISMO rate is also hard to square with its higher late and damage rates. Those would normally drive up other kinds of contact, which the paper doesn't report.

## Risks the recommendation leaves out

- **Peak season.** The contract starts on 1 October, straight into peak trading. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size. ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.
- **Heavier, fragile items.** 30% of Larkspur's parcels are lamps, mirrors and small furniture. ParcelLine's damage rate may be concentrated in that band, and the trial data could show whether it is.
- **Flexibility.** The 12-month term isn't unique to ParcelLine. SwiftDrop offers the same.

## Settled and open

**Settled by the paper's own figures:**
- ParcelLine misses the on-time and damage requirements.
- On total cost including damage and loss, SwiftDrop is cheapest, Meridian is about £1,100 a month more, and ParcelLine is about £8,000 a month more.

**Open, with what would settle each:**

| Question | What would settle it |
|---|---|
| Do carriers reimburse damage and loss? | The liability and claims terms in each contract. Reimbursement would lower the £48 figure, mostly for ParcelLine. |
| Is ParcelLine's damage concentrated in heavier items? | Damage by weight band from the trial data. |
| What actually reduced WISMO contacts? | ParcelLine's WISMO rate in April (before the text) compared with May. |
| How will each carrier perform at peak? | Peak-season references and performance data. |

## Recommendation

On the evidence in the paper, **SwiftDrop** is the better award. It meets every requirement, has the lowest total cost, offers a 12-month term and has peak experience.

**Meridian** is a reasonable alternative. It has the best on-time and damage figures at about £13,700 a year more. The trade-offs are the 24-month commitment and lost-parcel figures too small to compare.

**ParcelLine** should only be reconsidered if its contract reimburses damage and loss and it agrees to service levels that bring it within the 95% and 0.5% requirements. Even then, it would be taking its first peak season with Larkspur's heavier parcels.
